correctness.rationale: For all integers n≥3 and 1≤k<n, nontrivial triple cyclic rotations exactly swap unequal bits at distance one or two, identifying the channel with F_k(P_n²). A constructive occupied-to-vacant positive-flow arc reduction proves that the graph metric equals integral unit-cost transport; network-flow duality gives integer Lipschitz potentials. Two-connectivity of P_n² forces nonadjacent rises of the sorted potential values. Even and odd m=n−k window-sum bounds give the universal upper bound ceil(km/2). Complement symmetry handles k>n/2. Two explicit integer Lipschitz potentials and the endpoint-packed word pair yield the matching lower bound. Independently coded exhaustive all-pairs breadth-first verification over n=3..15 (110,998,233 ordered pairs) and all-pairs matching duality through n=9 (66,174 ordered pairs) agree. Finite computations are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The recent 2026 channel literature motivates binary three-position cyclic permutation errors but does not determine unrestricted sequential reachability. The result supplies an exact quadratic extremal number of local bursts for every length/composition and an explicit diametral pair, with a structurally motivated transport-dual argument. This is an all-parameter natural channel metric, not a small arbitrary case or a recomputation of known integer code-size tables. Does not claim code-size or decoding consequences beyond reachability.
